formulation: bounded call-graph reachability over CALL edges, from the standalone Master's driver-submission handler to the privileged process launch hosted on the DriverRunner surface
compile_status_convention: this field is written by the running script, so its presence is itself the evidence: a compile failure produces no envelope at all and the compiler's diagnostic lands in the console stream
run_status_convention: completed means every stage passed and the result region was emitted; failed is the only other value and is what the marker protocol reports instead, with no result region at all

failure_representation.marker_protocol: the query prints ---BLITZY-START--- before any work and brackets its result region with ---BLITZY-RESULT-BEGIN--- and ---BLITZY-RESULT-END--- only once every stage has passed, closing with ---BLITZY-OK---
failure_representation.on_failure_result_region: NO result region is emitted on failure: ---BLITZY-FAILURE--- is printed instead, the failing stage and the exception go to the console stream, and the exception is re-raised. A partial result region is never emitted, because one would read like a completed run
failure_representation.on_failure_measurement_fields: when compile_status or run_status carries its failure value, every measurement field - returned_record_count, returned_record_kinds, distinct_routes, spurious_count, bound_reached, bounds_reached, entry_points_discovered, entry_points_traversed, entry_points_truncated, walks, records and the graph counts - is null. Null is used consistently and no zero is ever written in its place, because a zero would read as a successful empty result and this query has a legitimate successful empty result to report
failure_representation.value_not_established_convention: a value that could not be established is named as such in the field that would have carried it, never omitted and never guessed: a value missing from the record is a value nothing downstream can check

distinct_routes_convention: routes from both walks deduplicated on (entry point, sink host, hop sequence); the walks' returns are never summed
distinct_routes_identity_function: a route identity is the triple (entry point method full name, sink host method full name, the ordered sequence of method full names from the entry point to the sink). Two returns with equal triples are ONE route however many traversal orders produced them, and the two walks below are deduplicated against each other on it rather than added together
spurious_definition: a route is spurious ONLY where it passes an authorization or ACL predicate before reaching the sink, the predicate set being exactly the five named selectors below; this judges the query, not Spark
spurious_definition_limit: the definition evaluates ONLY those five predicates. Any other conditional on the route is outside it and is NOT assessed by it: concretely, core/src/main/scala/org/apache/spark/deploy/master/Master.scala:411 if (state != RecoveryState.ALIVE) guards the branch that reaches createDriver at core/src/main/scala/org/apache/spark/deploy/master/Master.scala:417, and it is a recovery-state check rather than one of the five, so it is neither counted as a predicate nor reported as one. A spurious count of 0 therefore means exactly and only what the definition says, and does not mean that the route carries no conditional
expected_spurious_absence_statement: no route in the emitted set passed an auth/ACL predicate as defined by these five named selectors, and no call site of any of the five exists on the route surface at all, so the absence is structural rather than a consequence of the query filtering well
bound_value_meaning: MAX_CALL_DEPTH, the maximum call-graph hops walked from an entry point; it exceeds the hop count of the documented route, so a route absent within it is not an artefact of a short bound

bounds_meaning.MAX_CALL_DEPTH: maximum call-graph hops walked from an entry point
bounds_meaning.MAX_EXPANSIONS_PER_ENTRY: the per-entry-point step cap, counted in method expansions rather than in edges
bounds_meaning.MAX_TOTAL_RETURNS: the total-returns cap, across every record kind this query emits
bounds_meaning.MAX_ENTRY_POINTS: maximum entry points traversed; the remainder are counted as truncated rather than dropped silently
bounds_meaning.MAX_CALL_SCAN: cap on the indexed call-name sweeps used to find the sink and message call sites
bounds_meaning.FANOUT_CALLEE_THRESHOLD: a THRESHOLD rather than a cap: a call site whose resolved callee set is wider than this is recorded as a dynamic-dispatch fan-out site

bounds_reached_basis.MAX_CALL_DEPTH: reached: depth_bound_reached is true in both walks and max_depth_used equals 12 in both, so the frontier was still non-empty at the bound
bounds_reached_basis.MAX_ROUTES: not reached: route_cap_reached is false in both walks
bounds_reached_basis.MAX_EXPANSIONS_PER_ENTRY: not reached: expansion_budget_exhausted is false in both walks, the highest expansion count being 25009 of 200000
bounds_reached_basis.MAX_TOTAL_RETURNS: not reached: 4 records of 256, and total_returns_cap_reached is false
bounds_reached_basis.MAX_ENTRY_POINTS: not reached: 2 entry points discovered, 2 traversed, 0 truncated
bounds_reached_basis.MAX_CALL_SCAN: not reached: 1232 calls named start scanned of 200000, and the sweep reported truncated=false
bounds_reached_basis.FANOUT_CALLEE_THRESHOLD: exceeded, which is what "reached" means for a threshold: 86 fan-out sites encountered in the walk that follows them and 55 in the walk that records them without following

entry_points_truncated_meaning: the two counters exist so that a sweep cannot run unbounded and so that a trimmed traversal cannot pass for a complete one. A truncated count above zero is a measured property of the traversal, to be reported rather than hidden; it is zero here because 2 entry points were discovered against a cap of 16
entry_point_selection: BOUNDARY 4: the handler body compiles into a synthetic partial-function class, so the synthetic applyOrElse on every type matching ^org\.apache\.spark\.deploy\.master\.Master\$\$anonfun\$receiveAndReply\$\d+$ is selected together with the source-level org.apache.spark.deploy.master.Master.receiveAndReply

The bound was not loosened or removed, the query was not widened, and no route was manufactured

route_record_schema: walk_id - which of the two walks returned it

hop_count - the number of hops in the route
hops - the ordered sequence, each hop carrying from_method, call_site_callee, call_site_graph_line and to_method
passed_auth_or_acl_predicate - whether the route passed one of the five
spurious - the same value under the name the definition uses

graph.resolved_target: a host-shared read-only file outside the repository root, reached by following the symlink
graph.resolved_target_identification: no absolute host path is emitted anywhere in this envelope, so the resolved target is identified by the symlink-FOLLOWING byte size and sha256 below rather than by a host path. That pair is the identity of record and is what every load re-verifies; a host path would additionally vary between two checkouts of one branch and so could not be part of a deterministic envelope
graph.measurement_semantics: symlink-FOLLOWING. The named path is a small symlink, so measuring the link itself records a few dozen bytes rather than the graph: byte_size_without_following is recorded only to be discarded
graph.identity_record_role: the declared owner of this pair, which computed it at write time with the same symlink-following semantics; this envelope cites that measurement rather than establishing a second one
graph.identity_comparison_result: match - the observed byte size and sha256 equal the pair the identity record owns, on both values

runtime.command: JAVA_HOME="$JAVA_HOME_21" JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS=-Xmx64g SL_LOGGING_LEVEL=WARN joern --script queries/joern/01-callgraph-unguarded-driver-launch.sc -J-Xmx64g < /dev/null, invoked from a scratch directory outside the repository because joern eagerly creates ./workspace in its working directory and exposes no flag to move it
runtime.heap_direction_rule: the floor is a minimum and a default, never a ceiling: a larger heap is permitted and reported, and a smaller one is not, because a truncated result's silence cannot be told apart from a clean one
runtime.heap_override_mechanism: MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: joern's --script path forks a child JVM with no JVM options forwarded, so -J-Xmx reaches the launcher only and the child would otherwise run at an ergonomic default. JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS is inherited by the child and is what actually raises the heap the query runs at, which is why the query measures Runtime.maxMemory() and halts below the floor rather than trusting the flag it was given

runtime.heap_bound_jvm_position: 4 of 4 (frontend build, importCpg verification load, Stage 3 Joern runner, this probe)

predicate_selector.bytecode_constraint: a TYPE ANCHOR on org.apache.spark.SecurityManager, then an explicit exclusion of every name ending in the setter suffix _$eq, then an intersection with the exact five names above
predicate_selector.bytecode_collision_source: private var aclsOn at core/src/main/scala/org/apache/spark/SecurityManager.scala:59. Scala compiles a private var into accessors, so the graph carries BOTH a getter aclsOn() and a setter aclsOn_$eq(boolean), and both satisfy the acls.* alternative of the broad name regex. The setter is what the _$eq exclusion removes and the getter is what the intersection with the five removes
predicate_selector.over_match_hazards_note: each of these is a method on the anchored type whose name the broad regex reaches; the type anchor alone does not exclude them, and the intersection with the exact five is what does
predicate_selector.selector_set_widening_statement: the set is exactly these five and was not widened. Two auth-adjacent Boolean methods on the same type are deliberately NOT selectors: isEncryptionEnabled() at core/src/main/scala/org/apache/spark/SecurityManager.scala:280 and isSslRpcEnabled() at core/src/main/scala/org/apache/spark/SecurityManager.scala:295
predicate_selector.selector_block_comparability_reason: the selector set is held byte-identical across the three probe queries so that their three spurious counts remain comparable with one another. That comparability is the reason the set is constrained rather than convenient, and widening it in one query alone would silently make one count mean something the other two do not
predicate_selector.resolution_asserted_against: the graph, not the source: the query halts unless the three-step narrowing resolves to exactly the five names
predicate_selector.invocation_scope: the zero above is scoped to the ROUTE SURFACE and not to the program. None of the five is INVOKED in any of the three route files. It is not a claim that the five have no call sites: 18 call sites exist graph-wide in 18 distinct calling methods, and aclsEnabled() is invoked inside the anchored type's own source file. An unscoped "zero call sites" claim would be false
predicate_selector.route_files_searched_order: the source files corresponding to route_surface_type_prefixes, in that same order
call_sites_inside_the_anchored_type_itse: aclsEnabled() invoked at core/src/main/scala/org/apache/spark/SecurityManager.scala:407, inside the private isUserInACL declared at :402
predicate_selector.reference_is_not_invocation: a held reference is not an invocation. Every SecurityManager mention on the route surface is a reference of one of those kinds, and none of them invokes any of the five

records_order: an explicit TOTAL sort key: boundary records first, in the fixed boundary identifier order B1-rpc, B2-thread, B3-interface, B4-partial-function, then route records ordered by (walk_id, entry_point, sink_host, hop sequence). collection_order: every other collection carries an explicit order too, and which order depends on what the collection holds. Lists of SOURCE CONSTRUCTS ascend by pinned-tree source line - named_five_with_source_lines, over_match_hazards_excluded, launch_driver_calls and call_sites_inside_the_anchored_type_itself - and references_that_are_not_invocations is grouped by file in route order, the handler file then the sink file, ascending by line within each. Lists of GRAPH OR QUERY IDENTIFIERS ascend lexicographically: entry_points, sink_hosts, sink_call_sites, named_five, step1_broad_matches, step2_setters_excluded, step2_remaining, step3_non_predicate_residue_dropped, final_names, final_full_names, route_surface_type_prefixes, deliberate_non_selectors, selector_block_byte_identical_to, never_summed_with, effort_joern_api_constructs, api_constructs_only_here, api_constructs_only_there and non_deterministic_quantities_excluded. BOUNDARY lists follow the fixed identifier order B1, B2, B3, B4: records, boundaries_not_crossed, non_connectivity_hops and the boundary_verdicts lists. The four bounds objects follow the declaration order of the named constants in the query source. route_files_searched_for_the_five follows route_surface_type_prefixes, route_record_schema follows the field order of a route record, and evidence_relied_on follows the order the four kinds of evidence are listed in. records.reason: a message send is not a call: the sender enqueues a value on an endpoint reference and the receiving handler is dispatched later, so no CALL edge joins the two ends
records.modelling: modelled explicitly by pairing on the MESSAGE TYPE - call sites of org.apache.spark.deploy.DeployMessages$LaunchDriver.<init> are the producer end and call sites of its field accessors (driverDesc, driverId, resources) are the consumer end, with the message type's and companion's own generated machinery excluded by owning type

records.hop: org.apache.spark.deploy.worker.DriverRunner.start calls Thread.start(); the route continues in run() on the anonymous Thread subclass
records.reason: Thread.start() -> run() is a JVM scheduling relation, not a call: the start frame returns immediately and run() is entered on another thread, so no CALL edge joins them
records.modelling: not modelled - the two ends are reported as measured and the hop is left uncrossed

records.hop: the launch call site invokes the ABSTRACT ProcessBuilderLike.start; the JDK launch is reached only through the anonymous implementation
records.reason: an interface invocation names the declaring type, so linking it to an implementation needs the type hierarchy rather than the call's own name
records.modelling: not modelled by this query - whether the hop is crossed is a property of the graph's call linker and is reported as measured

records.hop: org.apache.spark.deploy.master.Master.receiveAndReply returns a PartialFunction whose body compiles into a synthetic class
records.reason: the method named receiveAndReply only constructs the partial function; the case bodies live in the synthetic class's applyOrElse, so a selector on the source-level name would traverse from a method that contains none of the route
records.modelling: modelled by selecting BOTH: the synthetic applyOrElse on every type matching ^org\.apache\.spark\.deploy\.master\.Master\$\$anonfun\$receiveAndReply\$\d+$, and the source-level receiveAndReply, so the difference between them is measured rather than assumed
